summary: Extends the IMAP command for listing mailboxes so that one extensible LIST command can carry options and return extra information. Previously each extension needed its own special list command, and combining extensions was awkward. This standards-track document gives clients a single, consistent way to ask for lists of mailboxes with added details.

plainLanguage.summary: Imagine asking a librarian for a list of shelves. Before, you needed a different form for each kind of question. Now there is one form with checkboxes, so you can ask for exactly what you want at once.

questions: how to list mailboxes with options in imap
subtitle: One extensible IMAP LIST command, with options, so every new way of listing mailboxes stops needing its own command.

tldr.problem: IMAP had two listing commands, LIST and LSUB, and each extension such as Mailbox Referrals had to add its function to both. Combining extensions meant adding yet more commands.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5258 extends LIST with multiple mailbox patterns, selection options in front, return options at the end, and extended data items in the response, all announced by the LIST-EXTENDED capability.
tldr.outcome: Clients can combine options such as SUBSCRIBED, REMOTE, RECURSIVEMATCH and CHILDREN in a single LIST command, and future extensions add options instead of commands.

today: RFC 5258 is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its header says it obsoletes RFC 3348 and updates RFC 2193.

sections.title: Why LIST Needed Extending
sections.content:
IMAP4 has two commands for listing mailboxes: LIST and LSUB. Each time an extension such as Mailbox Referrals needed a specialized list, it had to add its function to both commands, and those commands were not extensible. To make two extensions work together, yet another set of commands was needed, and the set grew with every new extension.

RFC 5258 fixes this by letting LIST carry options that are mutually compatible. The header of the RFC says it obsoletes RFC 3348 (the Child Mailbox Extension, whose CHILDREN feature is folded in here) and updates RFC 2193 (Mailbox Referrals).

The extension is identified by the capability string LIST-EXTENDED. By adding options to LIST, the RFC announces the intent to phase out and eventually deprecate the RLIST and RLSUB commands. LSUB is not deprecated, and clients that just need subscribed mailboxes SHOULD keep using it.
sections.plainLanguage: Mail programs used to need a new special button for every new way of listing folders. This RFC gives them one button with options instead.

sections.title: The Extended LIST Command
sections.content:
The new syntax is backward compatible and unambiguous. It is in use when the first word after the command name begins with a parenthesis (selection options), when the second word begins with a parenthesis (multiple mailbox patterns), or when the command has more than 2 parameters (return options). Otherwise the original syntax applies.

Three things change. Several mailbox patterns can be given in parentheses, and a name matching more than one pattern SHOULD produce only a single LIST response. Selection options go between the command name and the reference name and tell the server which mailbox names to select. Return options go at the end and say what information to return for each matched name.

An extended LIST MUST NOT treat an empty mailbox name as the special request for the hierarchy delimiter and root name; an empty string among several names is ignored. A server that does not accept a pattern MUST silently ignore it.

A client MUST NOT send an option the server has not advertised, and a server MUST answer an unrecognized option with a BAD response. Order does not matter, and an option repeated is treated as if it were given once. Return options MUST NOT cause the server to report additional mailbox names.
sections.plainLanguage: The old form had two blanks. The new one lets you add checkboxes before and after, and write several folder names at once.

sections.title: Selection and Return Options
sections.content:
The RFC defines three selection options. SUBSCRIBED lists subscribed names instead of existing mailboxes, and the list can include names of mailboxes that no longer exist. It is not the same as LSUB: with LIST (SUBSCRIBED) the attributes are accurate and complete, and \NoSelect keeps its normal meaning. Because some servers must do extra work to answer it, clients SHOULD keep using LSUB unless they want the extra information. REMOTE also shows remote mailboxes, replacing RLIST and, with SUBSCRIBED, RLSUB. RECURSIVEMATCH asks the server to also return parents that do not match but have children that do.

RECURSIVEMATCH MUST NOT be the only selection option (or be used only with REMOTE); the server MUST return a tagged BAD response. When several selection options are given, a mailbox must satisfy all of them, except where an option prescribes special rules, as RECURSIVEMATCH does.

Two return options exist. SUBSCRIBED returns subscription state for every matched name, with all flags accurately computed. CHILDREN asks for the child information from the old Child Mailbox Extension, and all servers MUST support it. The SUBSCRIBED selection option implies the SUBSCRIBED return option.
sections.plainLanguage: Selection options choose which folders appear, such as only the ones you follow. Return options choose what extra facts to print next to each folder.

sections.title: Attributes and Extended Data in Responses
sections.content:
The extension adds mailbox attributes: \NonExistent, \Subscribed, \Remote, \HasChildren and \HasNoChildren. \NonExistent says a name does not refer to an existing mailbox and implies \NoSelect. A non-existent name is only listed when it satisfies the selection criteria, or when RECURSIVEMATCH is given and it has a descendant that matches.

At most one LIST response should be returned per matching name, and attributes in one response are additive. For example, (\Subscribed \NonExistent) means the mailbox is subscribed but does not exist. Clients MUST treat a stronger attribute as implying what follows from it: \NoInferiors implies \HasNoChildren.

Responses may also end with extended data items, a parenthesized list of tagged data. Tags MUST be registered with IANA. The server MUST NOT return them unless the client has shown it supports extended responses, for example by using an extended LIST, and the client MUST ignore tags it does not recognize.
sections.plainLanguage: Each folder gets little labels like subscribed, or has subfolders. Labels can be stacked, and a program ignores labels it does not know.

sections.title: CHILDINFO and the CHILDREN Option
sections.content:
The CHILDINFO extended data item MUST NOT be returned unless the client specified RECURSIVEMATCH. It records the selection criteria that caused the response and signals that the mailbox has at least one descendant matching them. This replaces the way LSUB abused \NoSelect for the same purpose. Servers SHOULD suppress redundant CHILDINFO, returning a non-matching name only if at least one matching child is not also being returned.

Some servers let Customers/ABC exist without Customers. Such servers SHOULD signal a matching descendant to a client that did not use RECURSIVEMATCH with the pair \NonExistent \HasChildren.

The CHILDREN return option lets a client draw a collapsed folder tree, with a visual clue such as a plus sign, without issuing a LIST for every mailbox. With it, the server MUST return \HasChildren or \HasNoChildren, even if that is expensive to compute, and returning both is an error. \HasNoChildren is not the same as \NoInferiors, which says no children exist now and none can ever be created. Clients must cope with a \HasChildren mailbox whose children vanish or become inaccessible before they are listed.
sections.plainLanguage: CHILDINFO is a note saying a folder you did not ask about holds a match inside it. CHILDREN is the little plus sign telling you a folder has subfolders.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
Section 5 gives eleven examples. In one, a client lists top-level mailboxes with LIST () "" "%" RETURN (CHILDREN) and learns which have submailboxes without listing the second level. In another, LIST (REMOTE SUBSCRIBED) "" "*" mixes two selection options and is described as similar to RLSUB.

The RECURSIVEMATCH examples show the point of CHILDINFO. If only Foo/Baz is subscribed, LIST (SUBSCRIBED) "" "%" returns nothing, but adding RECURSIVEMATCH returns Foo tagged with CHILDINFO, meaning that Foo is not subscribed but has a child that is. Another example shows that CHILDINFO appears whether or not the matching children fit the pattern.
sections.plainLanguage: The examples show a program asking for folders in different ways and what the server says back each time.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The modified LIST has the same security considerations as LIST, LSUB, RLIST and RLSUB, which are covered in the IMAP4 specification (RFC 3501) and the Mailbox Referrals document.

The one new concern is child information. If a mailbox has children but the user cannot access any, the server SHOULD answer \HasNoChildren. A server that cannot compute this cheaply may answer \HasChildren and so reveal slightly more than intended. The RFC says this is usually not a concern, since a user for whom this is sensitive would not have been given access to the mailbox in the first place. CHILDINFO has the same considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: Saying a folder has subfolders you cannot open leaks a tiny hint. The RFC thinks that is usually harmless, because you would not be allowed near a secret folder anyway.

sections.title: IANA Registries for Options and Data Items
sections.content:
IANA has created two new registries: one for LIST-EXTENDED options and one for LIST-EXTENDED response data. Registration is done by sending a filled-in template by email. Names starting with V- are reserved for vendor-specific items, and each vendor-specific name MUST start with a registered vendor token. Names are case insensitive.

Registrations may not be deleted, only declared OBSOLETE. The IESG owns all items on the standards track. The registries start with the options SUBSCRIBED (selection and return), REMOTE, RECURSIVEMATCH and CHILDREN, and with the CHILDINFO data item.
sections.plainLanguage: There is an official list of all the checkboxes and labels, so nobody makes two with the same name.

cells: List subscribed names rather than existing mailboxes
Also return parents of matching children, with CHILDINFO
Report subscription state for matched names

items.label: Nonexistent
items.desc: The name does not refer to an existing mailbox; implies \NoSelect.

items.label: Subscribed
items.desc: The mailbox name is subscribed to.

items.label: Remote
items.desc: The mailbox is a remote mailbox.

items.label: Has no children
items.desc: The mailbox has no child mailboxes accessible to the user.

data.title: RECURSIVEMATCH with CHILDINFO
data.code:
C: C04 LIST (SUBSCRIBED RECURSIVEMATCH) "" "%"
S: * LIST () "/" "Foo" ("CHILDINFO" ("SUBSCRIBED"))
S: C04 OK done
